# Most examples from https://docs.rs/dateparser/0.3.1/dateparser/

# Sometimes the variables <TODAY>, <PST>, and <DAY> are used in expected values
# Patterns that do not indicate a date will vary in output each time this data
# is used. One strange pattern inserts the current day-of-month into a pattern
# specifying year and month.
 
# unix timestamp
1511648546	2017-11-25 22:22:26+00:00
1620021848429	2021-05-03 06:04:08.429000+00:00
1620024872717915000	2021-05-03 06:54:32.717915+00:00

# rfc3339
2021-05-01T01:17:02.604456Z	2021-05-01 01:17:02.604456+00:00
2017-11-25T22:34:50Z	2017-11-25 22:34:50+00:00

# ISO-8601
2026-09-18T01:02:03	2026-09-18 01:02:03+00:00
2026-09-18T01:02:03Z	2026-09-18 01:02:03+00:00

# rfc2822
Wed, 02 Jun 2021 06:31:39 GMT	2021-06-02 06:31:39+00:00

# postgres timestamp yyyy-mm-dd hh:mm:ss z
2019-11-29 08:08-08	2019-11-29 16:08:00+00:00
2019-11-29 08:08:05-08	2019-11-29 16:08:05+00:00
2021-05-02 23:31:36.0741-07	2021-05-03 06:31:36.0741+00:00
2021-05-02 23:31:39.12689-07	2021-05-03 06:31:39.12689+00:00
2019-11-29 08:15:47.624504-08	2019-11-29 16:15:47.624504+00:00
2017-07-19 03:21:51+00:00	2017-07-19 03:21:51+00:00

# yyyy-mm-dd
2021-02-21	2021-02-21 00:00:00

# yyyy-mm-dd 
2021-02-21 PST	2021-02-21 00:00:00-08:00
2021-02-21 UTC	2021-02-21 00:00:00+00:00
2020-07-20+08:00	2020-07-20 00:00:00+08:00

# hh:mm:ss
01:06:06	<TODAY> 01:06:06
4:00pm	<TODAY> 16:00:00
6:00 AM	<TODAY> 06:00:00

# hh:mm:ss z
01:06:06 PST	<PST> 01:06:06-08:00
4:00pm PST	<PST> 16:00:00-08:00
6:00 AM PST	<PST> 06:00:00-08:00
6:00pm UTC	<TODAY> 18:00:00+00:00
